name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,191

clue.text: Least expensive copy in treasury

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is held inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a treasury is where valuables are kept, like a strongbox or chest
to ape someone is to copy them

explanation.surface: Someone at the treasury hunts for the cheapest way to make a copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copy' reads as a noun, a duplicate document, but it is a verb meaning to imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapest is the superlative of cheap, meaning costing the smallest amount of money.

clue.text: Carbon put on iron oxide coating

blocks.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
rust is the reddish oxide that forms on iron

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: carbon is applied over a layer of iron oxide as a protective coating.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'put on' places C above RUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A crust is a hard outer layer formed over something, so it works as a synonym for a surface layer.

clue.text: Compel compliance with warden for ceremonial guards

indicators.note: to guard something is to keep it held within, so the letters are kept inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A warden makes ceremonial guards obey orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guards' looks like part of the scene, a noun for sentries, but it is a verb signalling that the answer is held within 'warden for ceremonial'.
explanation.definitionFit: To enforce a rule or law is to make people obey it, which is exactly compelling compliance.

clue.text: What aids digestion for every one left in steady state

indicators.note: one thing placed in another goes inside it, so a letter is set within a longer word

blocks.note: per means for every, as in miles per hour
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the standard abbreviation for left
stasis is a state of equilibrium with no change

explanation.surface: A health-food claim: something that helps digestion for everyone who is left in a steady condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for every one' reads as 'for everyone' but splits into two separate pieces, and the single letter for 'left' lands in the middle of the steady-state word.
explanation.definitionFit: Peristalsis is the wave of muscular contractions that pushes food along the gut, so it physically drives digestion.

clue.text: Boss, essentially odious, in workshop

indicators.note: the essence of a thing is its core, so only the central letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: a boss is a raised ornamental knob, as is a stud
the two central letters of this six-letter word

explanation.surface: A complaint about a hateful manager who works in the workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' wants to be a manager, but here it is the decorative knob on a shield or ceiling, which is a STUD.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is an artist's or craftsman's working room, so it is a near synonym of a place where things are made.

clue.text: When I start to assess land mass

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is taken

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
taken as written
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A surveyor says that is the moment they begin to evaluate a piece of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' reads as 'begin to', a verb phrase, but it selects only the opening letter of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent on Earth, and a continent is the biggest kind of land mass.

clue.text: Box containing electronic weapon

indicators.note: something containing another holds it inside, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: to box is to spar, as boxers do in training
E is the common abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A crate holding some high-tech weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container noun but is a verb, the sparring sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a long pole with a pointed tip, used for thrusting or throwing as an arm in combat or hunting.

clue.text: Not all of crybaby’s malevolence is terrible

indicators.note: taking only part of a phrase means the needed letters sit somewhere inside it

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A judgement that a whining child's spite is partly awful.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts inside the first word and ends inside the second; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal means extremely bad, as deep as an abyss, so it is a straight synonym of awful or dreadful.

clue.text: You flatter nun when drunk, alas

indicators.note: someone drunk is unsteady and muddled, so these letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone regretfully admits to sweet-talking a nun after a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole first three words are the letters to rearrange; 'alas' at the end defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, used just like the sentence adverb meaning that something is sadly the case.

clue.text: Fight roughly to stop change

indicators.note: a stopper is plugged into an opening, so one piece is pushed inside another

blocks.note: an alteration is a change
C stands for circa, Latin for about or roughly

explanation.surface: Someone resorts to violence to block a reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' looks like it describes the fight, but it is the abbreviation c. for circa, used before approximate dates.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy quarrel or scuffle, so it serves as a synonym for a row or dispute.

clue.text: Begin cycling for pastry dishes

indicators.note: going round in a cycle moves the first letter to the back

blocks.note: to begin is to start

explanation.surface: An instruction to get on a bike to go and fetch some pies.
explanation.walkthrough: The S at the front of START is moved round to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarts are open pastry cases with sweet or savoury fillings, so they are examples of baked dishes.

clue.text: Temporary setter’s following Italian football team

indicators.note: coming after something places this piece behind the other in the answer

blocks.note: Inter Milan is a famous Italian football club
the setter is 'I', so setter's means I am, written I'M

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler is only a short-term supporter of an Italian club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter's' is not possessive but a contraction: the setter says I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim means provisional or in the meantime, as with an acting manager filling a post briefly.

clue.text: Penny more naive, on reflection, before 1939?

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny
raw can mean inexperienced or naive

explanation.surface: Someone muses that Penny, looking back, was more innocent in the 1930s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name but is the coin abbreviation. The question mark flags that the definition is one example: 1939 is the start of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Prewar describes the period before a war; the years before 1939 are the classic case for the Second World War.

clue.text: Artist’s image as child incomplete

indicators.note: something incomplete is missing a part, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: pic is short for picture
taken as written
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A painter's portrait of himself as a boy was left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist's' reads as possessive, but the 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay. SON loses its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso, the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism, is one of the best-known painters of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Stones left on burial site

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is joined to its end

blocks.note: a grave is where someone is buried
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Pebbles placed on a tomb as a mark of remembrance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the custom of leaving small stones on a grave; here 'left' is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravel is a loose mass of small rounded pebbles, so it is a collective term for little stones.

clue.text: Polish Republican cuts Peter out

indicators.note: a cut goes into something, so one piece pushes inside another

blocks.note: to peter out is to fade away to nothing, to vanish
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A political story: a Republican politician from Poland axes someone named Peter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, but with a small p it is the verb or noun for a glossy finish. 'Peter out' is one phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnish is a glossy protective coating, and to varnish is to give a surface shine, like polishing it.

clue.text: Possible covering on mountain walk, primarily crucial if climbing

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters are taken
in a down clue, climbing goes upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a pace is a step or a walking speed
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Advice for a hike: what lies on a mountain path is vital to know if you are going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' fits the mountain scene, but in a down clue it means the letters are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice cap is a permanent sheet of ice over high ground; 'Possible' signals that not every peak has one.

clue.text: Quintessential conservative girl in charge

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a lass is a girl, mainly in northern British and Scottish use
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A description of the perfect example of a strait-laced woman who runs things.
explanation.walkthrough: Three short pieces in a row: the party abbreviation, a northern British word for a young woman, and the i/c abbreviation used on rotas.
explanation.definitionFit: Classic can mean typical or a perfect model of its kind, which is what quintessential means.

clue.text: Everything very regularly ignored in passage

indicators.note: skipping letters at a steady interval leaves only every other one

blocks.note: all means everything
dropping the first and third letters keeps the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A writer complains that everything is constantly overlooked in a piece of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passage' suggests a section of writing, but it is a narrow lane. The odd letters of 'very' go, leaving the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley is a narrow lane between buildings, so it is a kind of passageway one walks through.

clue.text: Missile found in cart with no head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so the first letter is lost

blocks.note: a barrow is a small hand cart

explanation.surface: A projectile turns up in a headless cart.
explanation.walkthrough: BARROW loses its leading B.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a projectile shot from a bow, and missile covers any object thrown or fired at a target.

clue.text: Wife to assist young dog

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
to assist is to help

explanation.surface: A spouse is asked to help with a puppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' only joins the two pieces; W is the standard abbreviation found in marriage records.
explanation.definitionFit: A whelp is a puppy, the offspring of a dog or wolf, so it names the animal at a juvenile stage.

clue.text: Clerics safe if developing altruism?

indicators.note: something developing is changing form, so the letters grow into a new arrangement

blocks.note: thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry question: are the clergy only secure if they are growing more generous?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is a loose fit: altruism and giving things up for others are close but not identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-sacrifice is giving up one's own interests for others, which is the core of unselfish concern for others' welfare.

clue.text: Semi-precious stone on end of calvary cross

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so just that one is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the closing letter of the word
an X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: A jewel set at the tip of a crucifix depicting the Crucifixion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' fits the religious scene, but it is just the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used in jewellery and carvings, a gem of modest value.

clue.text: Old stationer’s? Anyone can work there

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a stationer's is a shop selling writing materials, whimsically a pen shop

explanation.surface: A description of a traditional stationery business where any person may get a job.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a stationer's is described playfully as a place selling pens.
explanation.definitionFit: An open shop is a workplace that hires staff whether or not they belong to a trade union, so membership is no barrier.
